connections.why: Understanding what business is leads to planning and starting one
A business plan informs the choice of legal structure and ownership
Ownership form shapes which stakeholders hold influence
Objectives set by stakeholders drive the firm's strategic choices
The economic climate is a key input to strategic decision-making
The competitive environment shapes marketing strategy and positioning
Globalisation opens markets that reshape long-term strategy
Ethical and environmental pressures influence operations and quality choices
Market research evidence underpins marketing objectives and strategy
Strategy is delivered through decisions about the marketing mix
Segmentation and positioning determine how the mix is tailored
Product and demand decisions set the production methods required
Operational targets shape the choice of production method and capacity
Production methods determine how quality is managed and assured
Production scheduling depends on a reliable supply chain and stock
Pricing in the marketing mix draws on cost and break-even analysis
Securing appropriate finance is central to the business plan
Budgets and accounts together reveal financial performance
Financial analysis informs investment appraisal decisions
Investment appraisal supports major strategic decisions
Organisational structure affects how staff are motivated and managed
Recruitment and training set up the conditions for motivation
Motivated staff improve productivity and operational performance
Employees are a key stakeholder whose relations affect objectives
